page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 12 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 6 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and is equipped with 33 MB of L3 cache. It includes 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.u1-c1m4.3xlarge consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-focused tests, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1368.0 and a multi-core score of 7008.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 14790.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 635.15 GB/sec, which drops to 43.56 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The instance demonstrates solid throughput for standard operations, processing 11.32 million Redis SET operations per second and delivering 9.87 GB/sec in static web serving tests. However, it exhibits performance limitations on complex tasks; while it handles small 135M parameter LLM inference efficiently, its performance drops to the bottom 25% tier when processing a medium 7B parameter model, and it lacks the capacity for 70B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.u1-c1m4.3xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage provisioning. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as medium-scale web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput storage applications, or large-scale machine learning inference.
